class_to_concept_matrix._description: Soft-labeled matrix (15 classes x 18 concepts). Values in [0,1]. Most entries are binary (0 or 1) but transitional cell types use soft labels to encode within-class morphological heterogeneity due to maturation stage variation. BCE loss handles soft targets natively. Derived from Hoffbrand 2016 ch.1,8-10 and Briggs 2009 ch.2-4.
class_to_concept_matrix._note_soft_labels: Soft labels encode class-level proportions: fine_chromatin=0.3 means ~30% of cells of this type have fine chromatin. The concept constraint matrix still operates at the instance level: a single cell cannot have fine AND condensed chromatin simultaneously. These are compatible because the constraint shapes individual predictions while the soft label acknowledges the class contains a mix of maturation stages.
class_to_concept_matrix._note_zero_classes: Classes 13-15 (RBC/Platelet, Rare/Atypical, Artifact) have all-zero concept vectors because they either lack consistent morphological features or are not real cells.

row_justifications.myeloblast: Round nucleus, fine dispersed chromatin, 2-5 visible nucleoli, high N:C ratio, basophilic cytoplasm (Hoffbrand p.119, Briggs p.12). SOFT LABELS: agranular=0.7 / azurophilic=0.3 because AML Matek contains both Type I blasts (no granules) and Type II blasts (few azurophilic granules or Auer rods). The dominant pattern is agranular.
row_justifications.promyelocyte: Round nucleus, fine chromatin, DEFINING feature is abundant azurophilic (primary) granules, basophilic cytoplasm, largest cell in granulocytic series (Hoffbrand p.119, Briggs p.12). N:C ratio is moderate (not high) because the abundant granular cytoplasm is substantial. SOFT LABEL: visible_nucleoli=0.7 because nucleoli are prominent in early promyelocytes but fade as they mature toward myelocyte stage.
row_justifications.myelocyte: Round nucleus (may flatten on one side), nucleoli no longer visible, specific (secondary/neutrophilic) granules appear (Hoffbrand p.119, Briggs p.13). SOFT LABELS: fine_chromatin=0.3 / condensed_chromatin=0.7 because chromatin is actively condensing at this stage — early myelocytes retain partly open chromatin while late myelocytes approach metamyelocyte-like condensation.
row_justifications.metamyelocyte: Indented/kidney-shaped nucleus, condensed chromatin, no nucleoli, neutrophilic granules, low N:C ratio (Hoffbrand p.119, Briggs p.13).
row_justifications.band_neutrophil: Band/horseshoe-shaped unsegmented nucleus with parallel sides, condensed chromatin, neutrophilic granules, low N:C ratio (Hoffbrand p.119, Briggs p.13).
row_justifications.segmented_neutrophil: Multilobed nucleus (2-5 lobes connected by thin chromatin filaments), condensed/clumped chromatin, neutrophilic granules, low N:C ratio (Hoffbrand p.119, Briggs p.13).
row_justifications.eosinophil: Typically bilobed nucleus (encoded as multilobed), condensed chromatin, DEFINING feature is large orange-red eosinophilic granules filling cytoplasm, low N:C ratio (Hoffbrand p.122, Briggs p.16).
row_justifications.basophil: Bilobed nucleus often obscured by granules (encoded as multilobed), DEFINING feature is large dark purple-black basophilic granules, low N:C ratio (Hoffbrand p.122, Briggs p.17).
row_justifications.monocyte: Indented/folded/kidney-shaped nucleus, DISTINCTIVE fine lace-like chromatin (NOT condensed like granulocytes despite being mature), no visible granules at light microscopy level (fine dust-like azurophilic granules exist but not prominent), abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm, low N:C ratio, large cell (Hoffbrand p.123, Briggs p.18).
row_justifications.lymphocyte: Round nucleus, condensed/clumped chromatin in blocks, high N:C ratio (thin cytoplasmic rim), agranular cytoplasm, small cell (Hoffbrand p.127, Briggs p.19).
row_justifications.plasma_cell: Round nucleus pushed to cell periphery (eccentric), condensed clock-face/cartwheel chromatin, agranular, basophilic cytoplasm with perinuclear clear zone (Golgi), moderate N:C (Hoffbrand p.131, Briggs p.20).
row_justifications.erythroblast: Round nucleus, deeply basophilic cytoplasm, agranular (Hoffbrand p.24-25). SOFT LABELS: fine_chromatin=0.3 / condensed_chromatin=0.7 because AML Matek lumps all erythroblast stages — proerythroblasts have fine dispersed chromatin, while polychromatic and orthochromatic erythroblasts have progressively condensed/pyknotic chromatin. Most peripheral blood erythroblasts are at later stages, hence the 70/30 split. visible_nucleoli=0.2 because only proerythroblasts have prominent nucleoli. high_nc_ratio=0.6 because N:C ratio decreases as hemoglobinized cytoplasm expands in later stages.
row_justifications.rbc_platelet: Non-nucleated cells/fragments. No morphological concepts apply.
row_justifications.rare_atypical: Heterogeneous category. No consistent morphological profile.
row_justifications.artifact: Not a real cell. Damaged cells, debris, staining artifacts.

concept_constraint_matrix._description: Symmetric matrix (18 x 18). C[i,j] = -1 for biologically impossible co-occurrence, +1 for biological necessity, +0.3 for statistical tendency, 0 for no known relationship.
concept_constraint_matrix._sources: Hoffbrand 2016, Briggs 2009. Mutual exclusivities are physical impossibilities. Co-occurrences are either physical necessities (+1) or strong statistical tendencies (+0.3).

mutually_exclusive_pairs.reason: A nucleus cannot be both round and indented.
A nucleus cannot be both round and band-shaped.
A nucleus cannot be both round and multilobed.
Band = unsegmented, multilobed = segmented. Mutually exclusive by definition.
Opposite ends of chromatin maturation. A cell has one or the other.
Lineage-specific granules. A cell belongs to one granulocytic lineage.

cooccurring_pairs.reason: Nucleoli are only visible when chromatin is open/dispersed. Condensed chromatin physically obscures nucleoli. This is a physical necessity, not a tendency.
Both are blast features and tend to co-occur, but monocytes have fine chromatin with low N:C ratio. Soft positive, not hard.
Nuclear segmentation accompanies chromatin condensation in granulopoiesis, but lymphocytes have condensed chromatin with round nucleus. Soft positive.
